title: Work done by the compiler
description:
Write two `constexpr` functions so that a table of primes is computed **during compilation** and stored in the program ready-made.

- `constexpr bool isPrime(int n)`
- `template <std::size_t N> constexpr std::array<int, N> firstPrimes()`: the first `N` primes, in order.

Ordinary loops and local variables are allowed in `constexpr` functions. The tests use `static_assert`, so if anything cannot be evaluated at compile time the build fails.
hints: `isPrime` is the ordinary loop with `constexpr` in front; nothing in it needs a run-time library.
`firstPrimes<N>` fills a `std::array<int, N> result{};`: test numbers from 2 upwards and store each prime until N have been found.
